summary: Glacier County, MT ridgetop cabin built 1937 with a concrete and frame cab; sources differ on how much blew away in 1940; FFLA lists it gone; no source describes the site today.

facts.status_note: Sources differ on how much blew away in 1940; a 1969 photograph record shows remains

events.note: Concrete and frame cab per firelookout.com; built in 1937 per the Montana History Portal record
Upper floor blew away per the Montana History Portal record; firelookout.com says blown away three years after 1937. The extent of the loss is disputed between the two.
Photograph dated 1969-05-01 in the Glacier National Park Archives collection, captioned 'Remains seen here'

resolved_conflicts.explanation: firelookout.com says the lookout was blown away three years after it was built; the Montana History Portal record says only the upper floor blew away in 1940. The story reports both and does not choose between them.

sources.title: Two Medicine (Looking Glass) Fire Lookout Cabin

notes_for_editor: The 1937 build date agrees across two sources. The 1940 loss does not: firelookout.com says the lookout was blown away, and the Montana History Portal record says the upper floor blew away, so the story reports both. The FFLA coordinates (48.53677, -113.30135) are about 870 m from the firelookout.com location in the brief's conflict list, but the firelookout.com page read here gives no coordinates, so that conflict is not settled and the record was not changed. The brief kind 'ground' comes from FFLA; the Montana History Portal record mentions an upper floor, which could point to a two-story cab. Not changed, worth a check. The Forest Lookouts Glacier County page files the site as LOOKING GLASS (TWO MEDICINE) under the Blackfeet Indian Agency; not used. The Montana History Portal photo (HPF 9322) is a new find, but only its record page was read and no direct image URL was confirmed, so no photos entry was added. Used 2 WebSearch calls and about 5 page reads.
